description.en: This is the annual earnings threshold, computed as four times the PSS (Plafond de la Sécurité Sociale, the French social-security earnings ceiling), above which the 1.75% professional-expenses reduction no longer applies to the CSG (Contribution Sociale Généralisée) base — above this level the CSG is calculated on 100% of gross earnings instead of 98.25%. It is used in policy tinty_fr (personal income tax module) in the ArithOp computing the 'Amount of CSG - earnings' and the BenCalc computing 'Amount of CSG - unemployment benefits', and equivalently in the CSG policy tscxc_fr for the same two computations, always as a formula input alongside $csg_redrate. Per the taxes documentation, CSG is levied on 98.25% of current gross earnings until this four-times-PSS threshold, and on 100% above it.
